# Independent audit: saturated two-rate feasibility and exact support optimization

Audited all seven sections of `candidate 3b67f89e71aa7534`. **PASS.** The verifier `supporting computation verify_saturated_two_rate_contraction_two_sided.py` was read in the context of its stated scalar scope and rerun: **22,842 exact checks pass**. Its arbitrary scalar menus are not presumed to be realizable convex configurations. One wording repair in Section 7 was requested and applied: an initial supporting face need not survive as a set under contraction; what is proved and needed is preservation of its empty d-volume status.

## 1. Actual variation and one-sided inverses

Both homothetic contractions are about actual points of their bodies, so the new bodies are nested and remain compatible with the unchanged K. B's support changes exactly by -tv e_i, with e_i>=0. Pulling the A threshold back through its contraction gives beta_i+t(2z_i+u c_i+v e_i)+O(t^2), with the signs in (3) correct for every proper, full, and empty status. Proper K sections supply a strictly positive uniform slope bound. The scalar quantile construction therefore remains valid, including its O(t) estimates and one-sided section limits.

Solving R_i=-L gives (4). On an active branch, the threshold displacement has sign H_i and denominator k_i+2sigma_i; on an inactive branch it has sign H_i and denominator k_i. Thus the inverse hinge choices are consistent, including at zero. Each inverse has strictly positive slopes between 1/(k_i+2sigma_i) and 1/k_i. The inverse sum consequently has exactly one zero, and uniform expansions plus bounded difference quotients prove the actual common right derivative. Positive homogeneity also holds, including the zero rate pair as a formal limit.

## 2. Strict first-order descent and the finite rate test

The all-source certificate includes the middle menu and the tied B endpoint, while A's strict gap persists. Their normalized derivatives are strictly negative exactly under (7). For u>0, the B condition reduces to tau>a/(a+k); for u=0,v>0 it holds automatically. Since Phi is increasing in the loss argument, the menu condition is precisely the negative trial inverse sum in (9).

At that trial target every initially empty cut has H_i>0, so its negative-part hinge vanishes. Proper and exterior terms are affine in tau. Full-at-minimum terms are negative multiples of positive parts of affine functions, hence concave. Their intercepts A_i are negative and their slopes B_i positive, so there are finitely many positive breakpoints and a well-defined eventual linear slope. The displayed formula W_infinity(drb-J_infinity) is exact.

A continuous concave piecewise-affine function with finitely many breakpoints is negative somewhere to the right of tau0 exactly when its value at tau0 is negative or its eventual slope is negative. If both are nonnegative, all earlier slopes are at least the nonnegative eventual slope, preventing any descent below the initial value. This proves necessity as well as sufficiency for the stated strict certificate. The negative eventual-slope alternative is also exactly the actual B-only trial, so no infinite rate is required.

Scaling the boundary rates to (a+k,a) scales the trial loss to daQ, as asserted. The branch formula (15) is obtained by direct inversion, and all-proper specialization gives (16) with the correct factors d. The theorem concerns strict first-order decrease of this particular upper certificate, not all possible deformations or cases with vanishing first derivative.

## 3. Finite support-function optimization

For a full-at-minimum cut, active minus inactive inverse value is -sigma_i H_i/[k_i(k_i+2sigma_i)]. Its true inverse is therefore exactly the smaller of those two affine expressions. Summing these independent finite minima gives the minimum over the finite binary branch set Theta, proving (18). Proper terms have one branch; empty terms are inactive at the positive trial target for every actual p in A and q in B.

Expansion of c_i=beta_i-v_i.p and e_i=h_i-v_i.q gives exactly C_theta+(a+k)V_theta.p+aV_theta.q. Compactness of A and B and finiteness of Theta justify the attained joint minimum and its interchange. Minimizing the two linear forms gives the two support-function terms in (19), with the same vector -V_theta. If that formal branch is not selected at its support minimizers, the actual lower envelope is even smaller. Conversely, any negative actual value has a branch realizing it. Thus this optimization neither assumes freely selectable section weights nor combines unrelated maximizing centers.

The infinity weights are fixed by the cut statuses, independent of the contraction centers. Maximizing J_infinity over the actual B point q gives exactly the numerator in (20), including the plus sign on h_B(-V_infinity). The disjunction in (21) is therefore an exact existence criterion for actual centers and rates within the stated family.

## 4. Empty-status preservation and the actual loss envelope

At every initial level, the new A set is smaller and its threshold is higher, so f_i(s_i0,t)<=Q. The inverse sum at Q is nonpositive, giving q_menu(t)<=Q. For an initially empty A cut, f_i(s_i0,t)=Q exactly. Its meeting level is therefore no lower than s_i0, and its A threshold is no lower than beta_i. Since A_t is contained in A, that cut remains empty in d-volume. This includes closed max-support cuts and all boundary-face measures relevant to first-order limits.

Thus the actual loss L is nonnegative. On L>=0 all empty inverse hinges are inactive for any nonnegative rates and actual centers. The finite lower-envelope formula applies at the actual loss as well as at a trial target. At its zero,

    min_theta W_theta[L-uL_theta(p)-vJ_theta(q)]=0

means every branch is nonnegative and at least one is zero. This is equivalent to the exact maximum formula (22). It proves convexity, piecewise affinity, and positive homogeneity of the loss in the rates for fixed actual centers. It does not assert that any arbitrary branch is a physical response in advance.

The one-rate full-and-empty preservation lemma has a stronger conclusion than this two-rate statement: B's moving support can activate an initially full A cut here, so those full hinges are correctly retained. No such hinge is discarded merely by analogy with the one-rate case.
